question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
The evidence does not state a deadline for deciding whether to decline the offered position—it only gives a period for opting out of employment in the Institute.

- An officer or employee who "wishes to opt out of employment in the Institute, may do so within six months from the date on which he was offered employment" [629/2025 §33(2)(b)].
- Those who decline are paid compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme approved by the Minister and the Finance Minister [629/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: The text of §33 is cut off before any clause fixing a separate decision period after notification; that provision is missing from the evidence, so no such time limit can be confirmed.

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
Not less than **thirty days** before the current licence expires: the renewal application must be submitted "not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration of the licence previously issued" [657/2025 §6(1)].

- The request must be in the prescribed Form with the prescribed renewal fee [657/2025 §6(1)].
- The same wording appears in the Bill version 007/2026 (2026-01-20), later than the GS version 657/2025 (2025-12-12) [007/2026 §6].

Caveats: No committee-stage amendments are available; "prescribed" form and fee details are not in this evidence.

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
Notice may be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" that sufficiently identify the bill and intimate dishonour by non-acceptance or non-payment [601/2025 §8].

- The substituted s.49(5) replaces the previous subsection in full [601/2025 §8].
- The same text appears in 612/2025, 527/2024 and 552/2024 [601/2025 §8].

Caveats: The newest version is the Bill 612/2025 (2025-06-17); the quoted provision is from GS 601/2025 (2025-06-04), stated to be identical across those bills.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Society may "take and hold any property, movable or immovable," held "for the purpose of this Act" and subject to its rules, with power to "sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of the same" [047/2026 §13]; it may also acquire "lands or buildings" by purchase, rent, construction or renovation and deal with or dispose of them as the Council determines [047/2026 §6(a)], and administer "any real or personal property" via lawful trusts [047/2026 §6(f)].

- Property may vest "by virtue of any purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise" [047/2026 §13].
- Disposal of lands/buildings is "as determined by the Council" [047/2026 §6(a)].

Caveats: The GS version (041/2026, 2026-06-11) carries identical wording; I've cited the newer Bill.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The long title is changed by removing "and container operators", so the words "freight forwarders, non-vessel operating common carriers, and container operators" are replaced with "freight forwarders and non-vessel operating common carriers" [658/2025 §2].

- Later references are likewise replaced with "Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders and Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers Act" [658/2025 §3(1)(a)].
- The text is identical in the presented Bill [005/2026 §2].

Caveats: The Bill title still names container operators, but §2 (Bill, 2026-01-20) matches the GS text.

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2026 bill is the **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation)** bill, which incorporates an existing foundation as a corporate body with objects covering economic sectors and rural community development [043/2026 §2] [043/2026 §3].

- Objects include "developing, promoting, establishing, expanding or modernising all economic sectors in Sri Lanka" and empowering "rural, estate and underserved communities" [043/2026 §3].
- Two versions exist: Gazette version 043/2026 (15 June 2026) and presented Bill 055/2026 (27 July 2026), whose title spells "Recourses"; the quoted clause text is stated to be identical [043/2026] [055/2026].

Caveats: The evidence doesn't show whether other clauses differ between the two versions, and clause-level citations come only from 043/2026.

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
The evidence does state an age limit: a person is disqualified from appointment to the Board if they "is over seventy years of age" [613/2025 §9(i)].

- This appears in the disqualification list (a)–(i), alongside parliamentary membership and insolvency [613/2025 §9].
- The same clause appears in the GS version [594/2025 §9(i)]; the texts are identical, so GS and Bill do not differ here.
- Members otherwise hold office "for a period of three years" and may be re-appointed for "not more than two further terms" [613/2025 §10].

Caveats: the clause bars appointment by age; the evidence does not expressly say a sitting member must leave on turning 70.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The debts must be settled from the day the Act commences: all debts and liabilities of the Trust "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act, shall be paid by the body corporate hereby constituted" [009/2026 §12].

- This is from the Indira Cancer Charitable Trust (Incorporation) bill, GS dated 2026-02-05 [009/2026 §12].
- Note the near-identical 2021 bill, "Indira Cancer Trust (Incorporation)", uses the same wording [095/2021 §12].

Caveats: The clause fixes the reference day (the day before commencement) but states no payment deadline.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The evidence does not contain the new definition of “Director‑General”. It only shows the term replacing “Controller”/“Rubber Controller” [595/2025 §2], and bill-level summaries saying a new definition is “add[ed]” without quoting it [620/2025].

- §2(2) construes references in other laws/documents as “Director-General of the Rubber Development Department” [595/2025 §2].
- Newest bill: 620/2025 (Bill, 2025-07-09); identical §2 text in 595/2025 GS (2025-05-28).

Caveats: The defining clause itself is missing from the evidence; the auto-generated summary is a hint only.

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
A "qualified auditor" is defined in §10(4) of the bill: (a) an individual who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or any other institute established by law) and "possesses a certificate to practice as an Accountant" issued by that institute's Council; or (b) a firm of Accountants whose resident partners each meet that same membership and certificate requirement [597/2025 §10].

- Accounts are audited by a qualified auditor "appointed by Auditor General" under Article 154 of the Constitution [597/2025 §10].
- The bill's title matches; note the text also appears identically in 608/2025 [597/2025 §10].

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
The newest text is the **National Transport Commission (Amendment) - Bill, 592/2025 (2025-05-08)**, which inserts a new section 38A: the Commission computes fares using a formula it determines, adhering to "the national policy relating to transportation fares approved by Parliament, and specified by Order published in the Gazette" [592/2025 §19]. §5 also adds a power "to determine a formula to charge transportation fares after considering the written representations of the relevant stakeholders" [592/2025 §5].

- Commission "shall publish the lists of the transportation service fares … in the official website of the Commission" [592/2025 §19].
- Each provider "shall prepare a list … in accordance with such lists" and "cause such list to be displayed at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle" [592/2025 §19].
- The Commission "may inspect from time to time" compliance under s.39(2); failure is "guilty of an offence under section 40" [592/2025 §19].

Caveats: The evidence's §19 text cuts off mid-sentence, so the full 38A procedure (and the exact penalty in s.40) is not shown; identical wording appears in 577/2025 GS (2025-04-07) and 549/2024 GS (2024-08-28). Not legal advice.

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, the magistrate with jurisdiction over an approved detention centre must visit it "once a month" without advance notice, interview suspects and inspect detention records.

- Must "visit once a month", "interview the suspects and look into their well-being", and inspect registers and Detention Orders [078/2026 §33(1)].
- On torture allegations or signs, must "forthwith make an order" for examination by a Judicial Medical Officer [078/2026 §33(4)]; if satisfied on reasonable grounds, act under section 31 [078/2026 §33(5)].
- Must report non-conforming conditions to the Inspector General of Police [078/2026 §34(2)].

Caveats: The older Anti Terrorism Bill instead requires a "once a week" visit by the producing magistrate [444/2024 §32(1)]; the question's bill title matches only 078/2026.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
The evidence does not answer this: no passage deals with striking a company's name off the register, a restoration/reinstatement remedy, or escheat of a struck-off company's assets. The only related text amends s.487(5) on a struck-off company applying to court within "ten years" for re-registration and return of property vested in the State [582/2025 §17].

- Newest version: Companies (Amendment) – GS, 2025-04-24 [582/2025 §17]; earlier identical text 2024-08-06 [541/2024 §15].
- Caveat: the note's references to sections 484/484A do not appear in these passages, so I cannot confirm them; substantive striking-off provisions are missing from the evidence.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
The amended Section 23r(2) sets a fine of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees," plus "five thousand rupees for each day" the offence continues after conviction [032/2026 §18].

- The amendment replaces the old range of Rs 10,000–100,000 and daily Rs 500 [032/2026 §18].
- Conviction must be "before the Magistrate having jurisdiction" [032/2026 §18].

Caveats: This is a Bill (2026-05-06), text also in 026/2026; it shows the substituted wording, not the Act as consolidated.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The newest text is Bill 068/2026 (2026-09-08). It adds "methamphetamine" to the paragraph (a) list of named drugs and creates a new offence for manufacturing other listed drugs [068/2026 §2].

- New list wording: substitutes "heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine" [068/2026 §2].
- New paragraph (aa): manufacturing any dangerous drug in "Groups A, B, C, D and E in Part I of the Third Schedule" other than those five named drugs [068/2026 §2].
- Penalty: High Court without a jury, fine "not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees", or "not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years" imprisonment, or both [068/2026 §2].

Caveats: Identical wording appears in the earlier GS version 062/2026 (2026-08-24) [062/2026 §2]. The Third Schedule changes in §5 are not in the evidence, so how the listed drugs themselves are amended is unclear.

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The evidence does contain the Section 5 amendment: the GS bill (017/2026, 2026-03-03) amends s.5(1) to replace "sixty million rupees." with "sixty million rupees; or" and to close paragraph (c) at "prior to April 1, 2026", adding a new paragraph (d) [017/2026 §3].

- Paragraph (b) is amended only by deleting the trailing "or" from "hundred and twenty million rupees; or" [017/2026 §3(1)].
- Paragraph (c)'s date window becomes "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to April 1, 2026," [017/2026 §3(2)].
- New paragraph (d), "for any period commencing on or after April 1, 2026", sets four-quarter aggregate turnover not exceeding "thirty-six million rupees" [017/2026 §3(3)].

Caveats: The Bill version (023/2026, 2026-03-17) appears only as an auto-generated summary; its clause text is not in the evidence, so I cannot confirm it matches the GS text.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The amendment raises the retirement age for the judges covered by section 6(3) from "sixty-one years" to "sixty-three years" [058/2026 §3], and replaces section 6(4) so that "the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years" [058/2026 §3].

- It overrides the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355) for those other judges and magistrates ("Notwithstanding anything to the contrary") [058/2026 §3].
- Same clause text appears in the Bill version [064/2026 §3].

Caveats: The text doesn't name which judges fall under s.6(3); both versions appear (GS 2026-08-07; Bill 2026-08-18) with no difference shown.

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
Bill 596/2025, the Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Bill (presented 2025-05-08), creates the body corporate under that name [596/2025 §2].

- It was earlier published as a Gazette bill, 581/2025 (2025-04-10), with the same incorporating clause [581/2025 §2].
- Short title: "Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025" [596/2025 §1].

Caveats: No Act number or certificate date is in the evidence; committee-stage amendments are not covered.

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Bill 059/2026 (Bill, 2026-08-04) repeals the Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 [059/2026 §2]. An identical earlier version exists as 036/2026 (GS, 2026-05-15); text is stated to be identical.

- Short title: "Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Act, No. of 2026" [059/2026 §1].
- On commencement, the Chief of Defence Staff and Committee members "cease to hold such office" [059/2026 §3(1)].

Caveats: Cite by bill number; both versions match closely.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 604/2025, the National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) Bill presented 2025-06-03, amends section 3 of the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016 [604/2025 §2]. It is set to be "deemed to have come into operation on April 1, 2025" [604/2025 §1].

- A Gazette version also exists: Bill 586/2025 (GS, 2025-05-20), with the same clause text [586/2025].
- It sets the monthly floor at "twenty-seven thousand rupees" for April–December 2025, rising to "thirty thousand rupees" from January 2026 [604/2025 §2].

Caveats: Evidence mentions 586/2025 and 604/2025 only; the exact "No. of 2025" in the citation clause is blank in the text [604/2025 §1].

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The **Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment) Bill** — Bill 642/2025 (presented 2025-10-21), preceded by Gazette version 640/2025 (2025-10-02) — amends the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988 [642/2025; 640/2025 §2].

- It substitutes the levy brackets in section 2(1A): "ten per centum" retained, "fifteen per centum" for years from 1 April 2023 "but ending prior to October 1, 2025", and a new "(d) for any year commencing on or after October 1, 2025, at the rate of eighteen per centum" [640/2025 §2].
- It doubles the dollar charge in section 2(1AA)(b) from "United States Dollars fifty" to "United States Dollars one hundred" [640/2025 §2].

Caveats: Only summary-level text exists for 642/2025; the clause wording quoted is from the GS (640/2025). No other 2025 bill in the evidence amends the 1988 Act's levy rates.

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
The 2026 bill is **056/2026, Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) - Bill (2026-07-22)**, which amends the 1956 Act No. 47 [056/2026 §2]. An earlier GS version, 044/2026 (2026-06-25), has identical text.

- It substitutes "one hundred thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20a(3) [056/2026 §2][056/2026 §3][056/2026 §4].
- The higher penalties do not apply to offences committed before the Act comes into operation [056/2026 §5].

Caveats: The bill title does not name the 1956 Act; that link comes from the amending text itself.

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 650/2025, the Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Bill (Bill, 2025-11-14), amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008 (last amended by Act No. 12 of 2011) [650/2025 §2].

- It substitutes "ten years" for "twenty-five years" as the maximum tax-holiday period [650/2025 §2].
- It adds a one-month ex-ante cost-benefit analysis by the Ministry of Finance [650/2025 §3].
- The same text appears in GS 643/2025 (2025-11-07), the earlier Gazette version [643/2025].

Caveats: Only these two versions appear in the evidence; committee-stage changes are not covered.

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
The Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution (Bill 065/2026, presented 2026-08-18; earlier Gazette version 057/2026, 2026-08-07) amends Articles 107 and 137 [065/2026 §2][065/2026 §3].

- It sets Supreme Court retirement at "sixty-seven years" and Court of Appeal at "sixty-five years", with the Chief Justice retiring at 67 or after "a period of six years" in office, whichever is earlier [065/2026 §2].
- It raises the cap on other Supreme Court judges from "nineteen" to "twenty four" [065/2026 §3].
- The Sinhala text prevails in any inconsistency with the Tamil text [057/2026 §4].

Caveats: No other 2026 bill in this evidence proposes a twenty-second revision; the two versions' clause text appears identical.
